evidence.text:
Catching spirals early can be a game changer. I suggest finding music that produces the calming neurochemicals- I legitimately listened to Ellie Duhey's "money on the dash" on loop during a stressful move, and it was a LIFE SAVER. I wanted to watch something else while eating, and almost immediately started a spiral. Going back to what I now term the "Good Brain Music" stopped the spiral. 

I now maintain a YT playlist, adding new good music and removing mysic that no longer functions properly.

evidence.video_title: I’m a Psychologist. Stop believing every thought. Do this instead.
evidence.text:
@McGMumof3
One thought can change everything that follows.

The way you think shapes how you feel, what you do next, and the story you tell yourself. That’s why learning to work with your thoughts can change so much.

When I think I’ll fail → I feel fearful → I want to avoid → what helps is starting anyway.

When I think everyone is judging me → I feel anxious → I want to perform or hide → what helps is finding the evidence.

When I think I’m not enough → I feel low → I want to withdraw → what helps is one kind thing.

When I think I must be perfect → I feel stressed → I want to procrastinate → what helps is messy is fine.

When I think I’m behind → I feel deflated → I want to compare → what helps is zooming out.

When I think I’ve ruined everything → I feel ashamed → I want to shut down → what helps is one small repair.

When I think resting is lazy → I feel guilty → I want to push through → what helps is remembering rest is productive.

When I think I can’t cope → I feel overwhelmed → I want to freeze → what helps is the next step.

When I think nothing changes → I feel hopeless → I want to give up → what helps is one thing.

When I think I’m too much → I feel shame → I want to make myself smaller → what helps is remembering the right people won’t think so.

Your thoughts are not facts.
They are your brain’s best guess.
And your best guess can be updated.

evidence.video_title: I’m a Psychologist. Stop believing every thought. Do this instead.
evidence.text:
@McGMumof3
One thought can change everything that follows.

The way you think shapes how you feel, what you do next, and the story you tell yourself. That’s why learning to work with your thoughts can change so much.

When I think I’ll fail → I feel fearful → I want to avoid → what helps is starting anyway.

When I think everyone is judging me → I feel anxious → I want to perform or hide → what helps is finding the evidence.

When I think I’m not enough → I feel low → I want to withdraw → what helps is one kind thing.

When I think I must be perfect → I feel stressed → I want to procrastinate → what helps is messy is fine.

When I think I’m behind → I feel deflated → I want to compare → what helps is zooming out.

When I think I’ve ruined everything → I feel ashamed → I want to shut down → what helps is one small repair.

When I think resting is lazy → I feel guilty → I want to push through → what helps is remembering rest is productive.

When I think I can’t cope → I feel overwhelmed → I want to freeze → what helps is the next step.

When I think nothing changes → I feel hopeless → I want to give up → what helps is one thing.

When I think I’m too much → I feel shame → I want to make myself smaller → what helps is remembering the right people won’t think so.

Your thoughts are not facts.
They are your brain’s best guess.
And your best guess can be updated.

evidence.video_title: Stop Ignoring your behaviour. Heres what it’s actually telling you
evidence.text:
I’ve seen this creator, unfortunately, the name eludes me, who said that while the intent to do hobbies instead of doomscrolling is very appealing, the reality is that scrolling is a passive act of “leisure”, whereas doing a hobby is quite an active one and requires spending energy.
So, to combat that, she has a written list of things she’d like to be doing instead aka things that are passive enough to do when she’s tired. Like an adult coloring book or simple embroidery.
I tried the same and I can confirm it’s literally life-changing. I now have a list of things I want to \ could do & I keep them readily available. So when I catch myself spending a little too much time on social media, I will pick up the list and choose whatever draws me in the most that day. I’ve made so much progress in my hobbies & I’ve lowered my screen time significantly!
I thought I’d share this, since I also used to wonder what that advice really meant :)

When I think I’m behind → I feel deflated → I want to compare → what helps is zooming out.

When I think I’ve ruined everything → I feel ashamed → I want to shut down → what helps is one small repair.

When I think resting is lazy → I feel guilty → I want to push through → what helps is remembering rest is productive.

When I think I can’t cope → I feel overwhelmed → I want to freeze → what helps is the next step.

When I think nothing changes → I feel hopeless → I want to give up → what helps is one thing.

When I think I’m too much → I feel shame → I want to make myself smaller → what helps is remembering the right people won’t think so.

Your thoughts are not facts.
They are your brain’s best guess.
And your best guess can be updated.

evidence_appendix.text:
I’ve seen this creator, unfortunately, the name eludes me, who said that while the intent to do hobbies instead of doomscrolling is very appealing, the reality is that scrolling is a passive act of “leisure”, whereas doing a hobby is quite an active one and requires spending energy.
So, to combat that, she has a written list of things she’d like to be doing instead aka things that are passive enough to do when she’s tired. Like an adult coloring book or simple embroidery.
I tried the same and I can confirm it’s literally life-changing. I now have a list of things I want to \ could do & I keep them readily available. So when I catch myself spending a little too much time on social media, I will pick up the list and choose whatever draws me in the most that day. I’ve made so much progress in my hobbies & I’ve lowered my screen time significantly!
I thought I’d share this, since I also used to wonder what that advice really meant :)
